Class UDFFillTemplate

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.udffill.UDFFillTemplate
public class UDFFillTemplate extends Object
Parser and evaluator of the rule of the fill source TEMPLATE. A rule is one or more lines; empty lines and lines starting with # are ignored. A line may start with a condition [mic=XNAS,XNYS;currency=USD] followed by at least one space, the rest is text with placeholders {name|filter|filter(arg,...)}. The first line that produces a value wins: its condition matches, every placeholder is non-empty after its filters and the result passes the validation of the field. Any other line falls through to the next one. An instance is immutable and thread-safe; it is cached per field and fill rule version. The evaluation reads only the UDFFillContext and performs no I/O.

  • Method Details

    • parse

      public static UDFFillTemplate parse(String rule)
      Parses a rule. Lines are separated by \n or \r\n; leading and trailing whitespace of a line is removed.
      Parameters:
      rule - the rule as stored in fill_rule
      Returns:
      the parsed template
      Throws:
      UDFFillTemplateException - when the rule does not parse, naming line and position of the fault

    • evaluate

      public UDFFillTemplate.TemplateResult evaluate(UDFFillContext context, UDFMetadataSecurity field)
      Evaluates the rule for one security. Lines are tried in order; the first line that produces a value wins.
      Parameters:
      context - the master data of the security
      field - the field whose value is computed; its data type and field size validate each candidate
      Returns:
      the value or none, the line that produced it, and per line tried before the reason it fell through

    • legal

      public static String legal(String value)
      Removes parenthesised segments and legal-form words from a company name. A heuristic for building slugs, not an identification of the issuer.

    • validate

      public static String validate(String value, UDFMetadataSecurity field)
      Validates a candidate value against the field on an isolated one-key map, never on the stored values: with a one-field metadata list checkDataAgainstMetadata would remove every other key.
      Returns:
      null when the value is valid, otherwise the validation message
